description:
SURFACED by the fz-3sb adversarial audit (at 49126e966). fz-3sb correctly threads the real code_id into decode_token/decode_tokens so a token blob is decoded with ctx.code_id. But encode_tokens (token_payload.rs:9) bakes literal Vec<Token> payloads with REAL byte offsets ONLY during the initial parse of a submitted code's own text (called only from frontdoor.rs). derive_function_surface (jobs/source.rs:224) decodes an expanded function's token blob with expanded_source.code == FunctionSource.code (identity.rs:274) == the FUNCTION'S OWN defining code — which FunctionSourceExpander::expand (jobs/source.rs:401-430) never reassigns to the MACRO'S defining code (source.clone() swaps .source, not .code).

RISK: if a macro's quote-do-end body literally contains a type ascription / @spec / extern signature, and that quoted subtree is spliced verbatim into a caller defined in a DIFFERENT file (cross-module macro invocation IS supported — required_remote_macros / world.rs:943 run_macro_on_source), the baked token offsets belong to the MACRO's file but decode now uses the CALLER's code_id => Span = SourceId(caller) + offsets(macro file): an internally inconsistent span pointing at the wrong text.

STATUS: NOT confirmed reachable — needs nested quote-literal type syntax spliced through expansion WITHOUT re-parsing; the auditor did not trace to ground truth. NOT a regression from fz-3sb: the same scenario was already wrong before (SourceId(0) + offsets(macro file)); fz-3sb does not make a previously-correct case wrong.

TASK: (1) determine whether macro-spliced type/spec/extern tokens are a REAL reachable path (cross-file macro whose quote body has a malformed @type / type-ascription; observe the diagnostic span). (2) If reachable, thread the token's ORIGINATING code_id through expansion (carry it on the spliced subtree) rather than assuming the caller's. If NOT reachable, close won't-do with the evidence. VERIFY: a cross-file macro-spliced malformed type annotation points its diagnostic at the MACRO's file+offsets consistently. Related: fz-3sb, fz-ose.
title: Cross-code macro-spliced type/spec token blobs may stamp inconsistent spans (SourceId of caller + byte offsets of macro's file)
